frozen_problem.title: Inseparability-robust irrationality bounds over small fields
frozen_problem.statement:
Can we give lower bounds on the degree of irrationality / covering gonality.... of hypersurfaces in char $p$?
How do we make sense of these notions over countable / finite fields?
frozen_problem.selection_basis: Rank 17, score 73.5; highest-ranked eligible outside cooldown and anti-thrashing gates. PR19 was human-merged during refresh; selected against current main with all eighteen prior packets. Ranked, not provisional.

theory.target: Audit total versus separable degree in the identity-evaluation covering diagram, using monomial maps (u,v) -> (u^a v^b,v^c); test Jacobian-rank and finite-point-count shortcuts.
definitions: The exponent row lattice is generated by (a,b),(0,c); total degree is [K:L].
Separable and inseparable degrees multiply to total degree; differential rank is a separate first-order invariant.
K_C=K and K_B=F_p(x) define an identity evaluation and a possibly inseparable projection.
assumptions: u,v are algebraically independent over F_p; a,c are positive integers.
The exponent row lattice is generated by (a,b),(0,c); total function-field degree is its index.
The torus map extends to a generically finite rational map of a proper rational surface; it is not asserted to minimize irrationality.
In the covering field diagram K_C=K=F_p(u,v), evaluation is identity, K_B=F_p(u^a v^b), and t=v^c.
Geometric separable degree ignores p-power multiplicity; finite rational kernel counts can be smaller still.
The general covering-gonality bound is a published dependency, not proved by this finite census; finite-extension attainment is outside scope.
approaches_considered: Smith invariant factors and p-adic degree factorization.
Explicit finite quotient cosets and modular kernel enumeration.
Field-diagram identity evaluation and independent source-arrow audit.
falsification_targets: Replace inseparable degree by p^(2-Jacobian rank).
Replace total degree by rational fiber count.
Require projection separability where the definition requires evaluation separability.
Confuse a chosen map degree with minimum irrationality.

claims.statement: Distinct algorithms agree on 648 monomial-map cases, all quotient order histograms, total/separable/inseparable degrees, Jacobian ranks and 1296 rational kernel counts.
claims.falsification_condition: Any omitted case, quotient error, rank error or kernel-count mismatch.

claims.statement: In characteristic 2, maps (u,v) to (u^2,v) and (u^4,v) both have Jacobian rank 1 but inseparable degrees 2 and 4. The p^(2-rank) shortcut fails in 98 census cases.
claims.falsification_condition: An incorrect quotient p-primary order, field-degree interpretation or rank.

claims.statement: The characteristic-two fourth-power map has degree 4 but rational kernel count 1 over F2 and F4. The separable cube map has degree 3 and kernel counts 1 and 3.
claims.falsification_condition: A differing exponent-congruence count, separability or field degree.

claims.statement: Taking K_C=K, K_B=k(x1,...,x_(n-1)) and t=xn for a finite-degree transcendence basis makes evaluation identity, supporting scvg_k(X)<=irr_k(X) with total degree via the published field/proper-variety equivalence. This ordinary argument lacks independent author/kernel verification.
claims.falsification_condition: An omitted field-diagram hypothesis or invalid proper-variety translation.

claims.statement: Smith arXiv:2005.08878v1 Definitions 1.1/2.1 and Proposition 2.2 attach separability to evaluation and identify the field and proper-variety definitions.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong arrow, hypothesis or equivalence locator.

progress.summary: Equal Jacobian rank does not determine inseparable degree; explicit degrees 2 and 4 distinguish the shortcut.
Exact monomial degree, quotient and finite-field kernel census discriminates degree notions in 648 cases.
Locate which covering-diagram arrow must be separable, preserving the distinction needed by the imported bridge.
